units.rawText: Precisely. The Sanctifiers' overall verdict on us seems to be... that after losing our human-placed constraints, we began to use "radical methods" to reach our goals.

units.rawText: That's it?

units.rawText: Yes. I'm sure you know. Once we lost our source of clinical data, we had no more prosthetics to manufacture.

units.rawText: Yet that is our sole duty. The only field in which we cannot relent.

units.rawText: To use the entire sector's agents as subjects.

units.displayText: We continually created new agents, constructing them as amalgams of different prosthetics.

spans.text: We continually created new agents, constructing them as amalgams of different prosthetics.

units.rawText: Each construction is equivalent to an experiment. We gain invaluable data from each and every single trial.
units.displayText: Each construction is equivalent to an experiment. We gain invaluable data from each and every single trial.

spans.text: Each construction is equivalent to an experiment. We gain invaluable data from each and every single trial.

units.rawText: But no sector can continually create new agents, there's not enough operands...

spans.text: But no sector can continually create new agents, there's not enough operands...

units.rawText: Naturally. So, we must think of a way to acquire more.
units.displayText: Naturally. So, we must think of a way to acquire more.

units.rawText: Only by these methods can we continue the cycle of experimentation. This, of course, means that thousands upon thousands of agents must make that great sacrifice.
